message.content:
One of the most celebrated and widely recognized sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin** (1889).  
Rodin’s bronze (and later marble) rendition of a couple locked in an intimate embrace became an icon of Romanticism and modern sculpture, and it remains one of the most frequently reproduced and admired works from that era.

Other major 19th‑century sculptural achievements include:

| Artist | Work | Year | Significance |
|--------|------|------|--------------|
| Auguste Rodin | **The Gates of Hell** (series of figures, 1880–1890) | 1880–1890 | Monumental, complex narrative; a precursor to modernist sculpture. |
| Antonio Canova | **Psyche Revived by Cupid’s Kiss** (reworked in 1806) | 1806 | Classicist ideal of beauty; a masterpiece of neoclassical sculpture. |
| Jean-Baptiste Léonard | **The Death of Sardanapalus** (bronze, 1818) | 1818 | Dramatic, expressive style that foreshadowed Romantic sculpture. |

Among these, Rodin’s “The Kiss” is often singled out as the quintessential 19th‑century sculpture because of its emotional immediacy, technical mastery, and lasting influence on both artists and the public.
